content.text:
Before the map, one assumption stated plainly so it can be corrected cheaply: I'm planning the **linear algebra arc from almost scratch** — the goal recorded in your existing map. If this session's goal is something else, say so and I'll rewrite rather than adjust. ## The approach The field is usually taught backwards: matrices first, as arrays of numbers with a bizarre multiplication rule, and the geometry bolted on later as "applications." That order manufactures loose facts — you memorise that $AB$ multiplies row-by-column, that $\det = 0$ means no inverse, that eigenvectors are "special vectors," and none of it feels like it *had* to be that way. So this arc runs the other direction. It starts at the one unconditional truth the whole subject is generated by — that **linear algebra has exactly two moves: adding vectors and scaling them** — and derives everything else as forced consequences. Matrices, then, don't arrive as something you're handed; they arrive as *the only possible way to write down a map that respects those two moves*, and matrix multiplication is derived as what composition must be, not decreed. You may already be able to carry out several of these computations mechanically. That's fine and it's the point: those computations are the loose facts, and the session's job is to collapse them into the generator underneath. The order is: **geometry before algebra.** Vectors as arrows, then the coordinates that turn arrows into number-lists, then span and independence — which is where the first genuine "why" appears, since a basis will stop being a definition and become a language you choose. Only then linear maps, and only after that matrices. Determinants come late and geometric — a volume-scaling factor, so that "$\det = 0$" and "not invertible" turn out to be the same statement rather than two facts to memorise. Eigenvectors last, as the question the whole machine was built to answer: *which directions pass through unchanged?* Dependency structure: ```mermaid graph TD numbers[Real numbers: arithmetic rules] --> coords arrows[Vectors as arrows:
the two moves] --> coords[Coordinates:
an arrow is a list] arrows --> span[Linear combinations
and span] coords --> span span --> independence[Independence] independence --> basislang[A basis is a coordinate
system you chose] arrows --> linmap[Linear map:
respects both moves] basislang --> linmap linmap --> matrix[Every matrix
is a linear map] basislang --> matrix matrix --> compose[Composition is
matrix multiplication] linmap --> kernel[Kernel, image, rank] kernel --> inverse[Invertibility] compose --> det[Determinant:
volume scaling] inverse --> det matrix --> eigen[Eigenvectors:
directions that survive] det --> diag[Change of basis
and diagonalisation] eigen --> diag diag --> goal[One idea:
linear algebra = linear maps] ``` Two things to flag about the shape of this map. The bottom nodes are the ones I'll expect to be genuinely unconditional *for you* — arrows you can add and stretch, and the arithmetic of real numbers. Everything above them is earned. And the map is a hypothesis: if teaching shows you already hold something I've put high up, it gets pruned; if it shows a foundation is missing, a node gets added below. That rewriting is normal, not a failure of the plan. Accept it, or tell me what to change.

content.text:
The harness stores everything under one directory: `~/.config/LearnHarness/`. Most of it is Electron/Chromium junk that shouldn't travel. The actual state is one subdirectory.

## What to move

| Path | Contents | Move? |
|---|---|---|
| `data/graph/` | `nodes.jsonl`, `chains.jsonl`, `coverage.jsonl`, `positions.json`, `format.json` (version 1) | **yes** |
| `data/chats/` | your session transcripts — `chat_mwdj2lyq_…` (linear algebra) and `chat_mwdm7pj3_…` (this one) | **yes** |
| `data/jobs/` | two job records | yes |
| `data/plugins/` | installed plugins | yes |
| `data/settings.json` | app settings — likely includes API keys and model config | yes, but check it |
| `logs/main.log` | diagnostic only | optional |
| `auth.json`, `chatgpt-credentials.json`, `Cookies`, `Network Persistent State` | login tokens | no — sign in fresh |
| `Cache/`, `Code Cache/`, `GPUCache/`, `Local Storage/` etc. | Chromium caches | no |
| `SingletonSocket`, `DevToolsActivePort`, `.updaterId` | machine-local, break on copy | no |

So the transfer unit is `~/.config/LearnHarness/data/`. It's versioned (`format.json` says 1) — install the same app build on the other PC, `0.6.1`, or at least not an older one. A newer-format graph opened by an older binary is the one way this goes wrong.

## The commands

Close LearnHarness on the source machine first — `nodes.jsonl` and `chains.jsonl` are appended to at runtime, and copying mid-write can tear a line. Then:

```bash
tar -czf learnharness-data.tar.gz -C ~/.config/LearnHarness data
```

On the new machine, before launching LearnHarness for the first time (or after, but before using it — see below):

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/LearnHarness
tar -xzf learnharness-data.tar.gz -C ~/.config/LearnHarness
```

Then launch and check that `list_sessions` shows both chats and the 26 propositions.

Copy the AppImage too — `~/Applications/LearnHarness-0.6.1-x86_64.appimage`. The `.desktop` launcher points at that exact path, so either keep the same layout or edit `Exec=`.

## The one thing that will actually bite you

**Do this before using the harness on the new PC.** The graph files are not merged, they're overwritten — if the new machine has already accumulated its own `data/graph/`, extracting over it silently discards one side. If you've already used it there, stop and tell me; the two graphs need to be reconciled, not overwritten.

Second: don't copy `settings.json` blind if the two machines will differ in paths or you're rotating keys — read it first and adjust. Want me to open it and tell you which fields are machine-specific?
